title: The Layer War
dek: China just made the model a commodity. Satya Nadella saw it coming, Apple bet the company on it, and the bill lands on people who were never in the room. Us.
note: On a Thursday in July, a Beijing lab most Americans had never heard of released Kimi K3, a model that matched or beat America’s best on the work companies actually pay for, at half the price. Then it promised to give the thing away. Within a day, the chip index fell into a bear market, and the world’s most valuable company became Apple, the one that refused to build a frontier model at all.

This is the longest essay I’ve written, and it’s about the war underneath the melt: where AI’s money actually settles, who called it early (Satya Nadella did, in public), who bet catastrophically wrong, and who pays when the trillion-dollar promises come due. Someone always pays, and it is never the men in the room.
